### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/index.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35929be7d13bd98ca3d827f0517b17b7f01b74a9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `65c11b49c2416238aaeeabbf83cf589d83409002` — the merge of head `936f5755ce30a59edd7cd1dbc4558141108050d7` into base `35929be7d13bd98ca3d827f0517b17b7f01b74a9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 65c11b49c2416238aaeeabbf83cf589d83409002 && git checkout 65c11b49c2416238aaeeabbf83cf589d83409002
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 35929be7d13bd98ca3d827f0517b17b7f01b74a9 936f5755ce30a59edd7cd1dbc4558141108050d7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 35929be7d13bd98ca3d827f0517b17b7f01b74a9 && git merge --no-ff 936f5755ce30a59edd7cd1dbc4558141108050d7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 35929be7d13bd98ca3d827f0517b17b7f01b74a9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 35929be7d13bd98ca3d827f0517b17b7f01b74a9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Contract review of #32491 · 2026-11-12T05:22Z (TIER_DEFAULT sub-agent run by the seat, adopted by the seat)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `936f5755ce30a59edd7cd1dbc4558141108050d7`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

What I read: card #32155 (body, every comment, ruling B 6810282141, the Y′ claim amendment 6813607394), os-dev-report 6815324950, the PR #32491 body and its 8-file list, the net diff against main at this head, the check-runs on this head, and the fable analysis for the pre-patch readings. I built nothing and ran nothing.

**Which responses are compressed** (`response-compression.ts`, mounted by `adapter.ts` as the first `use('*')`, so it is the outermost middleware):
- **Coding.** br or gzip, chosen from `Accept-Encoding`. q-values are honoured, `q=0` refuses a coding, `*` covers codings the header does not name, br wins a tie. No header, `identity` or `deflate` alone gets identity bytes.
- **Threshold.** 1 KB. A declared `Content-Length` decides it. Without one, the body is read only up to 1 KB: a shorter body is re-sent as the same bytes, and a longer one is encoded from the bytes already read, so the whole body is never held in memory.
- **Types.** Hono's `COMPRESSIBLE_CONTENT_TYPE_REGEX`. `text/event-stream` is refused separately.
- **Never encoded.**
  - `res.write()` streams. The adapter marks them in `runHandler` before it resolves the response, so the middleware reads the mark after `next()`. The order is correct.
  - Any `Transfer-Encoding`.
  - An existing `Content-Encoding` (nothing is encoded twice).
  - `1xx`, `204`, `206`, `304` and `HEAD`. Range requests keep answering the identity bytes their `Content-Range` describes.
  - `Cache-Control: no-transform`.
- **Headers on an encoded answer.** `Content-Length` and `Accept-Ranges` are dropped. `ETag` passes through byte-identical. It stays strong across codings on purpose, so `If-Match` saves keep matching. That trade-off was in the PR that ruling B landed as it stood.
- **Observation, no defect.** A raw route returning a compressible `ReadableStream` with no `Transfer-Encoding` would be encoded without flushing. The fable analysis raised this. There is no such producer in the tree: the only one, the HMR route, is `text/event-stream` and also sends `no-transform`.

**The Vary rule** (`Accept-Encoding` is added unless already present, an existing `Vary` is extended rather than replaced, and `*` is left alone):
- It applies to every response of a kind the server could encode, whatever the request accepted and whatever the body size.
- After the patch round it is applied before the early return for `HEAD`, `206` and `304`, which is Y′ item 1.
- Gap: a `304` with no `Content-Type` gets no `Vary`, because the type rule cannot tell what its `200` would have carried. Both `304` producers in the tree are of this shape (`cli/src/utils/console.ts`, the stable-file branch; `runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts`). There is no cache-correctness effect, because a cache refreshing from a `304` keeps the stored `Vary`. The README, `http-protocol.mdx` and the changeset nonetheless say `304` answers carry `Vary` unconditionally. Nit; routed in ③.

**Opt-out and configuration.**
- There is no global switch, no plugin option and no environment variable. Ruling B answered the earlier opt-out question with option A: no switch.
- A route can opt out with `Cache-Control: no-transform`, or by setting its own `Content-Encoding`.
- `threshold` is an internal parameter. The module is not re-exported: `index.ts` re-exports `./adapter` only, and the two new adapter members are `private`.

**Robustness fix.**
- The zlib `data` handler now catches a failed `enqueue` (the reader has gone) and destroys the encoder. The replay source's `cancel` also destroys the encoder and cancels the body reader, so the encoder is released on both paths.
- No exception escapes, and later requests are served.
- It changes no surface and fixes a defect in the PR's own code, which was the Live E2E red. It is in scope under ruling B.

**Conformance snapshots: exactly Y′.**
- In both files, `content-encoding` joins `TRANSPORT_HEADERS`.
- `acrossDoors()` is applied to both sides of a cross-door comparison only: `hHead` against `sHead`, and the masked `viaDomain` against `viaMount`. It drops only the `accept-encoding` member of `Vary`, splitting the header into its members. Other members such as `Origin` are still compared. A `Vary` header is removed only when nothing else is left in it.
- The same-door assertion `sHead.headers` toEqual `sGet.headers` is unchanged, so it stays strict on `Vary`. Ignoring `content-encoding` there is required, because a `GET` can be encoded and a `HEAD` never is.
- Nothing else in the two files changed.

**Pins.**
- The unit `HEAD` test now asserts `Vary`. The PR body's ablation (moving the `HEAD` early return back above `Vary`) fails 1 of 24 tests, on that case. The same-door conformance pin catches the same regression independently: it was the red at 96151de2.
- The abort test drives a br answer and a gzip answer to their first byte, aborts each, and asserts no `uncaughtException` and a correct later gzip answer. The ablation that makes the guard rethrow fails 1 of 24, with `ERR_INVALID_STATE` for both codings. Both readings are the developer's; I did not reproduce them.
- Nits: no test asserts `Vary` on `206` or `304`, because they share the `HEAD` code line. The `encoder.destroy()` inside the catch is not pinned separately, because the cancel path also destroys the encoder.

**`createHonoApp`.** Untouched: there is no `packages/adapters/hono` path in the diff, and the hosted door gets no compression (Y′ item 3).

**Checks at review time.**
- Every required context that ran is green: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core 8/8, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Live E2E UI and Dogfood Regression Gate. Lint UI, Type Check UI and Build & E2E UI were skipped. Test UI passed.
- `Check Changeset` passed once. Its re-run, triggered by the PR body edit, was in progress.
- `PR-body guards` fails on both runs for one reason only: the duplicate-Fix error naming #32325, an open draft that also declares `Fixes #32155`. Its other three steps pass: closing-target-claim, partof-closing-keyword and single-claim-paths. There is also one non-failing warning, `UNDETERMINED`, because the newest claim-shaped comment on #32155 (amendment 6813607394) has no `Branch:` line.

### ② Semver level

- **`patch` is correct.** `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` is the only package with a changeset, and AGENTS.md says `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` is truthful.** Nothing a metadata author writes changes.
- **`Clause-②: no` is truthful, and the declaration should stay as written.**
  - The set of requests the server accepts is unchanged. Nothing accepted before is refused, so this is not a narrowing.
  - No export, option, environment variable or public member is added, so the public surface does not widen.
  - What changes on the wire is the representation, and only within what the client itself declared in `Accept-Encoding`. After decoding, the body, status and `ETag` are the same.
  - A client that sends no `Accept-Encoding`, `identity`, or `q=0` for both codings still gets identical bytes. The added `Vary` is cache-key metadata.
  - Dropping `Content-Length` and `Accept-Ranges` on encoded answers takes nothing away from Range clients: a Range request still gets an identity `206`.
  - An in-process caller of the public raw app that forwards `Accept-Encoding` now gets an encoded body. That caller is declaring the coding it accepts, so this is negotiation, not a change of contract. The changeset and README disclose it, and the three in-tree in-process callers drop or never forward the header.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Opt-out (open question from round 1).** Answered by ruling B: no switch.
- **Round 2's withheld security note.** Answered by ruling B. The round 3 report says `none`.
- **Out-of-scope finding 1: a `304` with no `Content-Type` gets no `Vary`.** The developer named no carrier ("as the seat sees fit"). It is not blocking (nit, see ①). Escalated to the seat for two things:
  - at ACCEPT, check the three prose sentences saying `304` answers carry `Vary`: they hold only for a `304` that carries a compressible `Content-Type`;
  - give the behaviour gap a carrier, either a small card or a note on #32155. #32536 does not cover it.
- **Out-of-scope finding 2: the hosted door neither compresses nor sends `Vary`.** Carried by follow-up card #32536, which covers the hosted side and its documentation, as Y′ item 3 asks.
- **Deviation 1: the file surface widened** to the two conformance files, the abort guard and its test. The two conformance files are authorised by Y′. The abort guard is a robustness fix to the PR's own encoder, made at the seat's request in the same round. The Y′ amendment does not name it. Suggest the seat note it on #32155.
- **Deviation 2: the PR body rewrite was handed to the seat.** Done: the body at this head carries the patch-round section.
- **Prose nit for the seat's ACCEPT.** The PR body's Tests section still says "23 cases" and has no bullet for the abort test. The head has 24 (13 cases plus 11 table rows), as its own patch-round section states.
- **Duplicate-Fix red.** #32325 is superseded by this PR and is closed by hand by the maintainer.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-94m481`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CaAUev5V62cLHhQwBi`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：自托管服务器（`plugin-hono-server`）默认按客户端的 `Accept-Encoding` 用 brotli/gzip 压缩 1 KB 以上的可压缩响应，流式响应、SSE、已编码、`no-transform`、HEAD、206、304 不压缩；可能被压缩的响应都带 `Vary: Accept-Encoding`。补丁轮另修了客户端中途断开压缩响应时进程会崩溃的问题。
- 为什么改：内置服务器原来不压缩，控制台 vendor 包约 2 MB 原样传输（#32155）。
- 风险与回滚：裁定 B 落地原改动，补丁轮按 Y′ 只加 HEAD/304/206 的 `Vary` 和两条一致性测试的跨门比较规则；托管门 `createHonoApp` 不动（#32536）。`Clause-②: no`，patch。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/response-compression.ts`；两份 http-conformance 测试里的 `acrossDoors()`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-hono-server exec vitest run src/response-compression.test.ts`，24 个用例全过。
- 需要你做的：先手动关闭 #32325（被本 PR 取代，且其代码含上述崩溃，不能合并），本 PR 的正文检查才会转绿；之后席位落地（落地动作若再被分类器拦下，会挂 `pm:awaiting-merge` 等人转 ready）。

席位意见：ACCEPT。按裁定 B（6810282141）落地原改动，补丁轮按 Y′（6813607394）。TIER_DEFAULT 评审 PASS（6815452954）。

## 席位核对

1. Shape: draft PR to `main`; `Fixes #32155` is its only closing keyword; it supersedes #32325. 8 files, +738/−6. The changeset `.changeset/32155-http-response-compression.md` is `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` patch, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
2. Premise measured: the original PR measured the 2 MB vendor bundle on the wire. This round reproduced the Live E2E red locally (the process exited after an aborted compressed response) and showed it gone after the fix, two local Live E2E runs at 17/17. Ablations: removing the HEAD `Vary` fix fails the HEAD case (1 of 24); making the abort guard rethrow fails the abort case with `ERR_INVALID_STATE` for br and gzip (1 of 24). Both restored.
3. Gates on head `936f5755`: every check-run `success` or an expected skip except `PR-body guards`, whose only error is the duplicate-Fix conflict with the still-open #32325; `Check Changeset` re-runs on the body edit. The dev's readings: plugin-hono-server 513/513, http-conformance 275/275, full dogfood VERDICT 0, 98 derived gate runs with 0 NOT-MEASURED, lint 0. K = 13 first-parent commits on `main` since the merge base `21667430`.
4. Accepted deviations: the file surface widened to the two conformance files (authorised by Y′) and to the abort guard and its test (a robustness fix to this PR's own encoder, made at the seat's request in the same round; noted on #32155). The PR body's test-count line is corrected to 24. Review nits: no `Vary` assertion on 206 or 304 (they share the HEAD line); `encoder.destroy()` in the catch is not pinned on its own.
5. Out of scope, filed: #32536 (the hosted door neither compresses nor sends `Vary`; platform or CDN duty) and #32565 (a 304 with no `Content-Type` gets no `Vary`, while the README, `http-protocol.mdx` and the changeset say every 304 does). Skills-docs: none.
6. Landing: `check-governed-merges --pr 32491` says NOT governed, 744 lines ≤ 3000. Tier S, not BREAKING. Held with `pm:awaiting-merge` until #32325 is closed by hand and `PR-body guards` turns green; the landing stroke was not attempted, since the auto-mode classifier refused it on #32464.
